milestone.title: harness command registry + mp agent harness surface

intent.outcome: A single typed registry maps each supported harness (opencode, pi, cursor for v1; the other herdr integrations behind herdr integration install) to its herdr agent start argv and per-harness flag translation (model, thinking level). mp watch and any future tool share one source of truth instead of each hardcoding launch commands.

problem.description: M149's B2 finding showed herdr agent start <name> -- <argv...> needs the full harness command, but the milestone left argv construction underspecified and scoped v1 to a hardcoded opencode/pi/cursor trio. As more harnesses are adopted (herdr ships 14 integrations), ad-hoc launch logic in mp watch will diverge. A registry + a small mp agent harness CLI surface (list, start-command <name>) externalises this so launch commands are discoverable and testable.

in_scope: HarnessRegistry type: harness name -> argv template + per-harness model/thinking flag mapping
mp agent harness list and mp agent harness start-command <name> subcommands
mp watch resolves [agent.runner].harness through the registry instead of a hardcoded match
Tests asserting each registry entry produces a valid herdr agent start argv
out_of_scope: Auto-installing herdr integrations (herdr integration install remains manual)

acceptance_criteria.description: A HarnessRegistry type maps each v1 harness (opencode, pi, cursor) to its herdr agent start argv template and per-harness model/thinking-level flag translation. Entries are data-driven (one struct per harness), not a hardcoded match inside mp watch.

design_decisions.choice: v1 ships opencode/pi/cursor only; other herdr integrations are behind herdr integration install + a future registry entry
design_decisions.rationale: Only those three have mp harness skills AND a locally-installed status bridge (herdr integration status). Expanding the registry is additive once an integration is installed and a skill exists.

design_decisions.choice: registry lives in the mp crate, surfaced via mp agent harness — single source for mp watch and future tools
design_decisions.rationale: Avoids each consumer (watch, raul, future dashboards) hardcoding launch commands. mp agent harness is the query surface; the struct is the internal source.

findings.description: probe: test if finding add works on reviewed-clean milestone
findings.author: external-review(M151-probe)

findings.description: F-02 — Dead test setup in harness_list_does_not_require_existing_plan (commands/agent.rs:189-199). The test allocates a TempDir + PlanContext but never uses them; the body only calls HarnessRegistry::v1() directly. Test name promises 'does not require existing plan' but does not exercise the CLI surface (which would actually verify the contract). Fix: drop the unused ctx setup, or actually invoke  against a fresh cwd without an existing plan_dir and assert exit 0 + 3-entry JSON.
findings.author: external-review(M151)

findings.description: F-03 — SUPPORTED_NAMES / V1_ENTRIES indexing drift risk (harness/registry.rs:50-58, 64-104). Doc comment claims a "compile-time check" but it is one-directional: adding V1_ENTRIES[3] forces SUPPORTED_NAMES to grow (otherwise index out of bounds), but adding to SUPPORTED_NAMES without extending V1_ENTRIES compiles cleanly. Real drift path: SUPPORTED_NAMES gains a 4th name -> WATCH_HARNESSES (alias) grows -> mp config set accepts the new name -> mp watch precondition calls HarnessRegistry::v1().get(new_name) which returns HarnessError::Unsupported -> inconsistent user experience (set succeeds, watch fails). Fix: invert the dependency (V1_ENTRIES declares ids; SUPPORTED_NAMES derives) or add a const_assert-style compile-time length check.
findings.author: external-review(M151)

findings.description: F-04 — runner_model_field_round_trips_into_harness_argv doesn't go through mp watch (tests/watch_config.rs:295-310). Test name implies AC-03 end-to-end coverage (the runner model config flows into the watch argv via the registry), but the body invokes `mp agent harness start-command opencode --model claude-opus-4` which only proves the registry produces correct argv. AC-03 is "mp watch resolves [agent.runner].harness and [agent.coordinator].harness through the registry to build the herdr agent start argv" — the test should at minimum assert that `mp watch --dry-run` reflects the configured model in the herdr argv (it currently does not; the opencode base case is covered by watch_dry_run.rs::dry_run_includes_herdr_start_argv_preview without --model). Fix: either rename to reflect what is tested (e.g. registry_emits_model_flag_for_opencode), or extend with a `mp watch --dry-run` assertion that includes --model in the argv.
findings.author: external-review(M151)

findings.description: F-05 — Stale doc comment on HarnessRegistry::iter (harness/registry.rs:117-122). Doc says "The cheap form (iter) is preferred over entries() for callers that just need name -> HarnessEntry mapping." but entries() does not exist on HarnessRegistry. Dead cross-reference. Fix: either drop the sentence or implement a public entries() that returns the static slice (or &[HarnessEntry]) with its own doc, then keep the comparison.
findings.author: external-review(M151)

findings.description: F-06 — resolve_harness_argv loses HarnessError source chain (watch/herdr.rs:78-80). The .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("{e}")) formats the HarnessError into a String and reconstructs an anyhow error, dropping the std::error::Error source. Callers cannot downcast_ref::<HarnessError>() or follow the source() chain for diagnostics. Fix: replace with anyhow::Error::new(e) (HarnessError already impls std::error::Error) so the original error type is preserved on the anyhow context chain.
findings.author: external-review(M151)
